file_roles.evidence: Interface declarations only: 'void persistHostMapping();' is added, '@Transactional' is removed from persist() and refresh(), and the now-unused Transactional import is dropped. Guice-persist applies @Transactional on the implementation, not the interface, so removing it here changes no behaviour.
A single visibility change, 'void persistHostMapping()' becoming 'public void persistHostMapping()', so the method can be reached through the interface. The method body is untouched.

'group.addHost(...); group.persist();' becomes a guarded, narrower call: 'if (! group.getHosts().containsKey(host.getHostId())) { group.addHost(host); group.persistHostMapping(); }'. Calling the full persist() re-persisted the config mappings as well, which is the path the trace takes into persistConfigMapping and removeAllByGroup.

rationale: The ConcurrentModificationException surfaces at 'ConfigGroupConfigMappingDAO.removeAllByGroup(ConfigGroupConfigMappingDAO.java:101)', a file no commit touches, while the fix lands four frames up in AmbariContext. The caller asked for more persistence than it needed, and the callee is where EclipseLink's change-set merge then blew up. The other two gold files only widen a method's visibility and declare it on the interface.
notes: Neither the file in the deepest frame nor ConfigGroupImpl.persistConfigMapping, the method actually named in the trace, is a causal target. A localizer following the stack trace lands on files that are either absent from gold or labelled refactor.
